GR9 a) FORWARD SEARCH: RelativeConnector.Start walks the SortedDictionary keys ascending for '==' (ContainsKey), '>' and '>=' and breaks on the first hit. GR9 b) REVERSE SEARCH: '<' and '<=' walk the same ascending key order but KEEP the last satisfying key and break on the first non-satisfying one — which is the largest RRN satisfying the relation, i.e. the first record found searching the file in reverse. ConditionBinder.MapOperator maps NOT LESS -> '>=', NOT GREATER -> '<=', GREATER OR EQUAL -> '>=', LESS OR EQUAL -> '<='; '!=' is unreachable here (SR3 rewrite in BindStart), and no other spelling can fall through the switch, so there is no silent no-match arm. OBSERVED, file with RRN 2/4/6: probe/rel-start/STPRB1 — KEY > 4 -> REC-6; KEY < 5 -> REC-4 (the LARGEST RRN below 5, not the lowest, proving the reverse search); KEY NOT GREATER 5 -> REC-4; KEY NOT LESS 5 -> REC-6; KEY = 3 -> '23' + INVALID KEY (GR9 c). probe/rel-ops/STPRBA — EQUAL TO 4 -> REC-4; GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO 5 -> REC-6; LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO 5 -> REC-4; >= 5 -> REC-6; <= 5 -> REC-4; LESS THAN 1 -> '23'; GREATER THAN 9 -> '23'. probe/empty-start/STPRBC — KEY >= 1 on an empty relative file -> '23' (GR9 c). The compiler gates the OTHER half of that same sentence -- READ ... PREVIOUS raises COBOL0900 at --std 85 (VersionConformancePass.cs:254, Constructs.ReadPrevious2002) -- and gates every other post-85 element of START (start-first-last-2002, start-with-length-2002, both with constructs.json rows). One arm of the rule verified at four editions, the other at three and ungated at the fourth => PARTIAL.
